header: L9 · The delivery manager who has seen hundred-task plans · sonnet
verdict: No prior finding of mine has status A or M (all three are parked for stage B). The delta leaves plan.md untouched, so it trails the spec in the pr package path (Required) and in three smaller rules (Advisory).

findings.section: plan.md T005 (title, Verify line, Acceptance); 10 10.2 (run step row); 12 12.4
findings.defect: The write pass moved pr into its own main package, tools/ci/pr, run as go run ./tools/ci/pr, with a go list -deps test of its import closure. T005 still names the step tools/ci pr, its Verify runs go run ./tools/ci pr <payload file>, and no acceptance line holds the import-closure test.
findings.scenario: T005 is built from its lines: pr becomes a subcommand of tools/ci, the Verify command is green, and the pr job's run line (go run ./tools/ci/pr) is refused by the new run step row or builds the whole tools/ci closure; the isolation the package split was made for is never tested.
findings.change: In T005 rename the heading, change the Verify command to go run ./tools/ci/pr <payload file>, and add an acceptance line: a go list -deps test fails when the closure of ./tools/ci/pr holds a package outside the standard library and the paths on approvals. Line 68 of the task template can keep tools/ci pr only with a note that it means that package.

findings.defect: The removing resume now depends on a fingerprint written with the removing state and recomputed on a rerun, but T068 has no acceptance line for a rerun of rm or recreate on a removing generation (resume when the fingerprint is equal, salvage again when a worktree changed).
findings.scenario: T068 passes on its listed cases; the rerun compares only heads, as before the delta, and a file added to a worktree between the two runs is deleted with the sandbox.
findings.change: Add to T068 two lines: a rerun on a removing generation with an unchanged fingerprint resumes at sbx env rm; one with an untracked or ignored file changed salvages again first.

findings.section: plan.md T087 and O7; 10 10.5 (fuzz run counts only on schedule)
findings.defect: Pre-tag now counts only a schedule-event fuzz run, and fuzz.yml runs once a day; neither T087 nor O7 says so, so a candidate whose build inputs changed waits for the next cron with the operator idle and nothing in the plan telling the agents to start the tag earlier.
findings.scenario: O7 starts after the last change to a fuzz target; --pre-tag fails for want of a newer scheduled run; the operator waits up to a day, or dispatches the workflow by hand, which does not count.
findings.change: T087 gets a line for the daily schedule cron and the schedule-only rule, and O7 notes that the last change to the fuzz inputs lands at least one day before it.

findings.section: plan.md T093 to T096 (gh attestation verify); 12 12.1 (gh floor 2.68.0); 09 J1
findings.defect: The gh floor 2.68.0 and the Probe B1 record of the gh version are in the spec, and no task holds the floor or the record (the plan mentions only the git floor and tools/release verify).
findings.scenario: J1 is written for a floor no code or probe checks; an operator with gh 2.60 gets an unknown-flag error, which B1 never recorded.
findings.change: Add to the task that writes B1 (or T020) a line that the result records the gh version, and to the tools/release verify task that a gh below the floor fails with a message naming it.
